simple.meaning: יְבַל (yᵉbal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to bring.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 5:14. Its contexts include kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְבַל (H2987).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יְבַל (yᵉbal) / H2987 is traced through Ezra 5:14, Ezra 6:5, Ezra 7:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H2987. yebal [ יְבַל ] verb Haph`el bear along, carry (see Biblical Hebrew); — Perfect 3masculine singular הֵיבֵל , accusative of thing + ל location Ezra 5:14 ; 6:5 ; Infinitive לְהֵיבָלָה 7:15 , accusative of thing.

occurrences.englishText: The gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple that was in Jerusalem, and brought into the temple of Babylon, those Cyrus the king also took out of the temple of Babylon, and they were delivered to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.

Also let the gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, be restored and brought again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put them in God’s house.
and to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem,
